timeline.title: Massive Protests Erupt in Czech Republic Against Public Media Funding Overhaul
timeline.summary: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs gathered in Prague to protest against the government's proposed changes to public media funding. The plan aims to eliminate mandatory license fees and shift funding to the state budget, which critics argue could increase government control over media. Organizers estimated the crowd at around 350,000, marking one of the largest protests in the country's history.

Concerns over increased government control of media

timeline.title: Czechs Protest Government's Media Funding Overhaul in Large Numbers
timeline.summary: Tens of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on November 15 against a government proposal to cut public media fees and shift funding to the state budget. Critics argue that this change threatens the independence and viability of public broadcasters. Protesters expressed concerns that the lack of safeguards against political influence could undermine democracy, drawing parallels to historical events like the Velvet Revolution of 1989.
key_facts: Tens of thousands protested in Prague on November 15.

Critics claim the plan threatens media independence and democracy.

event_overview.title: About Central African Republic Protests
event_overview.subject: Central African Republic Protests
event_overview.summary: The Central African Republic protests are a cost-of-living and civil-liberties mobilization centered in Bangui in November 2026. Demonstrators called for lower fuel prices and the release of civil-society figures detained after an earlier October shutdown action; the main reported march was organized by the opposition Republican Bloc for the Defence of the Constitution (BRDC).

facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: The reported large march took place in Bangui, the Central African Republic’s capital, on November 13, 2026; coverage of the event was published on November 14.

facts.label: Organizers
facts.value: The march was called by the BRDC, an opposition coalition. A United Nations Secretary-General report identifies the Republican Bloc for the Defence of the Constitution as a coalition of opposition parties.

facts.label: Core demands
facts.value: Protesters sought a reduction of petrol prices to 850 CFA francs per litre, from reported prices above 1,100 CFA francs, and called for the release of five civil-society leaders arrested after an October strike action.

facts.label: Form of action
facts.value: The November march was reported as authorized and was monitored by Central African security forces and United Nations peacekeepers from MINUSCA.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the November 2026 Bangui protest over living costs and detentions; the separate November 15 Czech Republic media-funding protest is not part of this Central African Republic event.
